name: Maryland Crab Cakes

cookwares.name: large cast iron skillet or nonstick skillet

ingredients.name: lump blue crabmeat, picked over for shells
vegetable oil, plus more as needed

instructions.primary_message: In a large mixing bowl, combine half of crabmeat with mayonnaise, panko, egg, mustard, Worcestershire, Tabasco, and paprika. Season with salt and pepper and stir until thoroughly combined.
Gently fold in remaining half of crabmeat until just combined; try not to break apart the lumps of meat any more than necessary as you stir.

If pan-frying, form crab mixture into patties and arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet. In a large cast iron or nonstick skillet, heat oil (and/or butter) over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add patties and cook, rotating and flipping occasionally for even browning, until browned and crispy on both sides, about 10 minutes. Lower heat at any point to prevent burning, and add more oil or butter as needed if pan goes dry.

If broiling, line a rimmed baking sheet with foil and preheat broiler. Form the crab mixture into handball-size balls and mound on the prepared baking sheet. Broil about 13 cm from the broiler element until well browned on top and heated through, about 4 minutes.
Serve right away with lemon wedges and tartar sauce, if desired.

schema_metadata.keywords: crab, crab cake, crabmeat, essential, fish, Maryland, seafood, shellfish

description: Maryland-style crab cakes shouldn't be loaded up with an excess of filler. This recipe keeps the focus squarely on the crab.
notes:
Optional or for serving: Lemon wedges, for serving; Tartar sauce, for serving (optional)

Optional substitutions: vegetable oil → unsalted butter
author: Daniel Gritzer
